title: MovenRun documentation
description: MovenRun is a movement game. Cover ground on a hexagonal map of the real world, hold the cells you cross, and keep them by coming back.

title: How it works
description: The MovenRun loop: cover ground, claim the cells your route crosses, hold them by coming back, and build districts out of what you keep.
keywords: how it works cover ground, claim the cells you cross, and keep them by coming back. four verbs, and the whole game sits on top of them. move walk, run, or cycle. all three count the same. tap once and you are moving within seconds, with distance, time, and pace kept glanceable so your attention stays on the road. pause and resume whenever you need to. there is no minimum speed and nothing to tap mid session. one session, end to end. it loops back on returning, so tomorrow's walk starts here. capture the world is divided into hexagonal cells, each about 0.74 square kilometres, using h3. every point on earth falls in exactly one cell, and the cell is the same for every player. two people standing on the same corner are standing in the same cell, in lagos or in leeds. finishing a session claims the cells your route crossed. that is the moment a walk becomes a foothold. hold a claimed cell d

title: Territory and deeds
description: What a MovenRun cell is, how holding and decay work, how districts build out of held ground, and what a deed adds at launch.
keywords: territory and deeds the world is a hexagonal map, and every cell on it is ground somebody can hold. move to take it, come back to keep it. what a cell is a cell is one hexagon of the real world, roughly 0.74 square kilometres, indexed with h3. hexagons rather than squares because every hexagon borders six others at equal distance, so adjacency behaves the same in all directions. that matters in a game about spreading out from ground you already hold. cells nest. a group of them makes a district, districts make a city, and one grid runs from a single street to a citywide season. holding and losing ground strengthens when you return and comes under pressure when you do not. every held cell carries a defense meter and a control meter. defense drains from the moment you stop visiting. control only starts to drain once defense is empty, so a cell you visit even occasionally stays firmly yours

title: Movement and privacy
description: How MovenRun checks that a route really happened, and why the system never stores your coordinates.
headings: We do not store your coordinates
keywords: movement and privacy a game about ground has to know the movement was real. it does not have to know where you live. checking a route a recorded route becomes a proof, or it gets rejected. every route runs through the same checks before it counts for anything. plausibility. a route has to move at speeds a person can actually move at. anything implying a vehicle is rejected. signal quality. positions with poor accuracy are dropped, and a route made mostly of poor fixes is rejected rather than guessed at. continuity. a route needs enough points, close enough together, to describe continuous motion. teleports between two ends of a city do not pass. uniqueness. each route reduces to a deterministic fingerprint. submit the same movement twice and the second one is rejected, and routes that overlap in time with one already accepted are caught the same way. the checks run on our servers rather

title: Onchain
description: The MovenRun deed, toll, and supply design: one deed per cell, tolls paid to holders, and a capped $MOVE schedule issued against verified movement.
keywords: onchain movenrun's contracts run on base sepolia while the economy is tested. mainnet at launch. what follows is the design those contracts implement. deeds one deed per cell. a deed is held in the player's own wallet, carries the cell's provenance and defensive strength, and can be transferred directly. holding it is what entitles you to the tolls the cell earns. deeds are issued against ground already held in the game, so the supply of them is bounded by the map rather than by demand. a cell that goes dormant long enough is reclaimed and reopened, which keeps abandoned ground in circulation instead of permanently locked up by somebody who stopped playing. tolls every time $move is issued for movement through a cell, a share of it goes to that cell's deed holder rather than to the mover. that is the toll, and it is what turns a held cell from a badge into a small piece of infrastructure

title: Roadmap
description: What MovenRun is building and in what order: the movement game, the deed registry on mainnet, the live economy, and community governance.

keywords: frequently asked questions straight answers about what movenrun is and how it works. what is movenrun? a movement game. you walk, run, or cycle, and the hexagonal cells your route crosses become ground you hold. keep visiting and the ground stays yours. stop, and somebody else takes it. do i have to be fast? no, and the design goes out of its way to make sure of it. holding ground comes from returning to it rather than from pace or distance, so the strongest players are the most regular ones. a twenty minute walk on a tuesday morning, every tuesday morning, beats one long weekend run. can i lose ground i have taken? yes. every held cell has a defense meter that drains while you stay away, and once it empties your control over the cell starts draining too. visiting restores it. that pressure is the point, because ground nobody can lose is not worth holding. what happens to my location dat
